# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual gives a light-to-wire mapping, but I cannot speak it. Deaf must first establish a shared gesture code for the four color words while speaking those color names aloud, so I can later gesture the required wire color back to Deaf. I should wait for Deaf’s setup. 

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I can feel one large button embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE and three wires in positions 1, 2, and 3. Their tactile properties are not otherwise distinguishable to me.
Deaf says to Mute: Bomb view: display reads 0. Light is blue. Large button says PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires in order: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Please consult manual and instruct Blind.

The blue light maps to the yellow wire. Deaf sees yellow as wire position 3. A three-finger gesture can convey that position directly to Deaf, who can then tell Blind to cut wire 3.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display 0; blue light; button says PUSH TO DEFUSE; wires are position 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Please give the exact safe action.
Deaf says to Mute: I received your gesture. Blind cannot see it; I relayed its hand-shape description. Please signal the exact required physical action in a clear, describable sequence if that gesture was not itself the instruction.

The earlier hand shape was ambiguous. The required action is to cut the third wire, not press the button. I can only convey this to Deaf visually, so I will use three repeated pointing gestures as an explicit count; Deaf can relay “cut wire 3” verbally to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "👆", "👆"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf saw your gesture as thumb, index finger, and little finger extended, but does not know its meaning. I cannot see gestures. Please tell me the exact action in words: push, or cut wire position 1, 2, or 3.
Deaf says to Mute: I see your sequence but cannot safely infer it. Please send an unambiguous gesture-based instruction for Blind: identify whether to press the button or manipulate a wire, which numbered wire if applicable, and any count or hold duration. I will describe each gesture aloud exactly.

No gesture has yet been assigned a meaning, so I cannot safely encode “cut wire 3” merely by choosing hand shapes or repetitions. Deaf can speak to me, so Deaf must first state a gesture code aloud—for example, one symbol meaning “cut” and distinct symbols meaning positions 1, 2, and 3. Once that code is stated, I can send the corresponding symbols back for Deaf to relay verbally to Blind.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Do not rely on the earlier gesture instruction yet. Deaf correctly says no action code exists. Please wait for Deaf to establish an unambiguous gesture code with you, then repeat your manual instruction using that code.
Deaf says to Mute: To make this safe, please use a redundant signal: for button action, send repeated closed-fist/pushing-like gestures; for a wire, first show the wire number with raised fingers, then a cutting-like gesture. Repeat the complete instruction twice. I will relay the hand-shape descriptions to Blind.

Deaf has now established a describable protocol: show the wire number with raised fingers, then a cutting-like gesture, twice. The safe wire is position 3, so I will send the three-raised-fingers sign followed by the scissors-like sign, repeated exactly.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "✌", "🤟", "✌"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Use this code for your next instruction: 👍 means PUSH; ✂ is unavailable, so 👎 means CUT. After the action symbol, show wire number as ☝ for 1, ✌ for 2, or 🤟 for 3. For PUSH, show only 👍 three times. Repeat the complete sequence three times.
Deaf says to Mute: I can relay numbers but need the operation too. Please gesture a clear action depiction followed by its target: e.g. an open palm pressing downward for the button, or a scissors/cutting depiction for a wire; then show the wire number with fingers. Repeat once. Your current 3-2-3-2 pattern is ambiguous to Blind.

The agreed explicit code says 👎 means CUT and 🤟 means wire 3. The manual’s blue-light mapping selects the yellow wire, which Deaf identified as position 3. I will send the complete coded instruction three times.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "🤟", "👎", "🤟", "👎", "🤟"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures: [👍 👍 👍 👎 ☝ 👎 ✌ 👎 🤟]
Deaf says to Mute: I saw Blind's signal: three thumbs-up gestures; then thumbs-down with one raised index finger; thumbs-down with a V/two-finger hand; thumbs-down with the thumb-index-little-finger hand. I relayed your latest repeated thumbs-down-plus-three-finger signal to Blind exactly.
Deaf says to Mute: Please make the intended operation physically explicit and repeat it: button press versus wire cut/pull, then the target number. I will immediately describe it to Blind.

The safe action remains to cut wire 3. To make the operation visually depict cutting rather than relying on the thumbs-down code Deaf did not receive, I will use the scissors-like two-finger gesture followed by the three-finger wire number, repeated.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🤟", "✌", "🤟"])
```
